scope: LESSONS_ONLY: title/tagline/job relevance, 8 outcomes, 35/35 theory/reference paragraphs, 9 theory code/output blocks, 9 callouts, 2 figures and 1 Theory playground. I Do / We Do / You Do / self-check / exams excluded.

meta_leak.source_only_note: Filename/id performance-extreme are legacy stable URL/progress identifiers; do not rename without migration.
meta_leak.learner_facing_topic_drift: REJECTED: unlike S37, the performance-extreme Theory playground is on-topic, but it contains technical contradictions and false evidence captured as findings.

research_basis.use: CPython 3.13+ supports optional free-threaded builds where the GIL is disabled and threads can use multiple cores.
Default GIL-enabled CPython serializes Python bytecode, but free-threaded builds exist and performance libraries may release the GIL.
Many NumPy operations release the GIL and can benefit from thread-level parallelism; object dtype is a counterexample.
ProcessPoolExecutor uses multiprocessing, bypasses GIL and requires picklable callables/arguments/results; actual transport is not json.dumps length.
Queue maxsize bounds number of items, not bytes; full/qsize are advisory and put_nowait/Full is the safe rejection signal.
wait_for cancels the awaitable and waits for cancellation completion; asyncio.timeout cancels current task and translates cancellation to TimeoutError outside the context.
Log/trace correlation uses execution trace context including TraceId and SpanId; a custom correlation string alone is not an emitted trace.
Sensitive PII should generally not be logged directly; remove/mask/sanitize/hash/encrypt and prefer de-identification when identity is unnecessary.
Error budget is evaluated over a compliance window; release freeze follows budget exhaustion, not every instantaneous metric threshold miss.
Each objective has an error budget defined from its SLO over a stated period; policy applies when budget is exhausted.

research_basis.source: AWS Builders Library: Making retries safe with idempotent APIs
research_basis.use: Recording idempotency token and mutating operations must be atomic/consistent/isolated/durable to avoid token-before-effect and effect-before-token failure windows.
example.com/.org are reserved for documentation; example.pe is not an IANA example domain.

rejected_findings.claim: Queue.full() being advisory is omitted from main theory.
rejected_findings.evidence: Main T2-A explicitly teaches full() as advisory and recommends put_nowait+Full; the defect is that the Theory playground contradicts this rule.
A bounded item queue can block/reject producers and is a valid backpressure mechanism; it is simply not a byte/RSS memory cap.

rejected_findings.claim: Processes are never suitable for CPU-bound work.
rejected_findings.evidence: For pure-Python CPU-bound work on the ordinary GIL-enabled build, ProcessPoolExecutor is appropriate; the defect is categorical routing of all CPU/vector work.

rejected_findings.claim: The source is wrong that asyncio.wait_for cancels on timeout.
rejected_findings.evidence: Current asyncio docs confirm cancellation; the executable defect is that S38 never actually uses wait_for/timeout and therefore tests no cancellation.

rejected_findings.claim: Idempotency key must change on every retry.
rejected_findings.evidence: The source is correct that retries of the same logical operation should use the same idempotency identity; the defect is persistence/atomicity and version intent.

rejected_findings.claim: Retry with exponential backoff is bad practice.
rejected_findings.evidence: Bounded retry with backoff/jitter for transient failures is standard; the defect is that the router retries every non-poison kind and the executable omits real bounds/deadline/jitter.

rejected_findings.claim: Logs, metrics and traces are not legitimate observability signals.
rejected_findings.evidence: They are standard observability signals; the defect is that S38 creates one dict and calls that logs+metrics+traces.
It is registered and correctly illustrates the effect→crash→retry uncertainty window; it actually exposes the canonical checkpoint code's contradiction.

rejected_findings.claim: Legacy id performance-extreme should be renamed immediately.
rejected_findings.evidence: Source documents it as stable URL/save key; content mapping is on-topic and migration risk is real.

findings.summary: S38 treats S37 measurement discipline as usable although S37 remains REPAIR_REQUIRED and its benchmark harness is not machine-valid.
findings.attack: Concurrency choices and SLO numbers can be justified by invalid or handwritten timings.
findings.defense: Conceptually building concurrency after profiling is correct.
findings.fix: Require repaired BenchmarkManifest/BenchmarkResult and S37 regression gates before using performance evidence.

findings.summary: No S38 artifact binds concurrency comparisons to fixture hash, code/config, stage boundary, environment fingerprint and equivalence oracle.
findings.attack: Changing executor can change ordering/state/result while looking faster.
findings.defense: The prose repeatedly says measure first.
findings.fix: Reuse a versioned manifest and compare baseline/candidate behavior plus latency/throughput/error/queue/resource metrics.

findings.summary: The lesson states CPU-bound CPython threads will not help because one thread executes bytecode, without bounding the claim to the default GIL-enabled build or pure Python.
findings.attack: CPython 3.13+ has optional free-threaded builds; current Python docs explicitly qualify the GIL rule.
findings.defense: The default CPython build remains GIL-enabled and pure-Python CPU work is usually process-bound.
findings.fix: Teach interpreter/build/library boundary and measure rather than infer from CPU label alone.

findings.summary: Dense/vector scoring is routed mechanically to processes even though many NumPy operations release the GIL and can run in parallel threads.
findings.attack: Processes may add serialization/copy cost and oversubscription while threads may be faster for native numeric kernels.
findings.defense: Some CPU work remains pure Python and benefits from processes.
findings.fix: Benchmark the actual kernel and library threading behavior; do not map vectorized=processes.

findings.summary: measure_bound uses arbitrary ratios and accepts zero, negative, NaN and infinity as operational evidence.
findings.attack: CE01-CE03 show invalid metrics produce io/cpu/mixed decisions.
findings.defense: The helper is intended as a toy decision heuristic.
findings.fix: Validate finite nonnegative measurements and present ratio thresholds as an explicit local heuristic, not diagnosis.

findings.summary: Outcome promises threads/processes/async and pools, but theory only returns plan strings and never runs ThreadPoolExecutor, ProcessPoolExecutor or asyncio.
findings.attack: No concurrency, cancellation, ordering or worker failure is observed.
findings.defense: Avoiding heavy pools in browser is reasonable.
findings.fix: Use local-python artifact/tests for at least one real executor and async timeout path; browser can remain conceptual.

findings.summary: ProcessPool serialization/IPC cost is represented by len(json.dumps(payload).encode()).
findings.attack: ProcessPoolExecutor requires picklable objects and uses multiprocessing serialization/transport; JSON length neither measures that serialization nor IPC latency/copy cost.
findings.defense: Comparing compact vs bloated payload size is still a useful intuition.
findings.fix: Measure pickle serialization size/time and actual executor round-trip for the exact payload, or label JSON only as an approximate independent payload-size exercise.

findings.summary: The lesson reintroduces ana@example.pe.
findings.attack: example.pe is not an IANA reserved documentation domain and can represent a real external domain.
findings.defense: It visually looks synthetic.
findings.fix: Use ana@example.com or ana@example.test consistently.

findings.summary: Theory and figure call Queue(maxsize) a memory cap.
findings.attack: Python defines maxsize as an upper bound on number of items, not bytes/RSS; one huge item or worker-held payloads can still exhaust memory.
findings.defense: Bounding item count often bounds queue growth if item sizes are separately constrained.
findings.fix: Call it an item-count/backpressure bound and add payload-size/RSS budget if claiming memory protection.

findings.summary: The lab TokenBucket never refills, yet the contract claims no more than R tokens per window.
findings.attack: It enforces a lifetime quota, not a time rate/window; after two calls it denies forever.
findings.defense: The paragraph explicitly acknowledges that limitation.
findings.fix: Either rename to fixed quota and narrow the criterion or implement monotonic-time refill/window behavior.

findings.summary: The mutable token counter has no synchronization and no 429/Retry-After behavior despite a concurrency/rate-limit contract.
findings.attack: Concurrent check/decrement can violate shared rate state on interpreters/runtimes without global serialization; provider feedback is never consumed.
findings.defense: Single-thread toy calls are deterministic.
findings.fix: Use a concurrency-safe limiter/ownership model and test 429/Retry-After or explicitly exclude provider feedback from the lab.

findings.summary: The Theory playground uses if q.full(): else q.put(), directly contradicting T2-A's own safe guidance.
findings.attack: Python docs and S38 itself say full() is advisory; another producer can fill between check and put.
findings.defense: The playground runs sequentially so the demo happens to be deterministic.
findings.fix: Use put_nowait/Full or timed put in the playground too.

findings.summary: fetch_with_timeout only compares a supplied latency number to a threshold; it never waits, times out or cancels work.
findings.attack: A declared 200 ms provider returns immediately, so cancellation semantics cannot be observed.
findings.defense: The comment clearly calls it a simulation.
findings.fix: Add an actual asyncio.wait_for/timeout local coroutine and assert cancellation/elapsed behavior; keep pure classifier only as policy helper.

findings.summary: Resource cleanup is proved by assigning closed=True to a local boolean in finally.
findings.attack: No socket/file/context-managed resource exists; close_in_finally=True is also a literal returned before cleanup.
findings.defense: It demonstrates that finally executes.
findings.fix: Use a tiny closable fake that records close(), or a real local context-managed resource, and assert post-condition outside the function.

findings.summary: Timeout classifier accepts negative and non-finite latency/timeout values.
findings.attack: CE04-CE05 show negative timeout and NaN/negative latency produce plausible timeout/ok states.
findings.defense: Nominal fixture uses valid values.
findings.fix: Reject non-finite, negative latency and non-positive timeout before routing.

findings.summary: The roadmap/tagline requires tested handling of a slow provider, but no theory artifact actually blocks a worker, times out a call or demonstrates pool recovery.
findings.attack: Changing latency_ms changes a branch only, not elapsed time/resource occupancy.
findings.defense: The conceptual policy is present.
findings.fix: Induce a local slow coroutine/fake service, measure queue/worker effects, cancel it and prove subsequent work progresses.

findings.summary: scored_event returns one dict containing a nested metric and calls that logs+metrics+traces.
findings.attack: No logger emits, no metric aggregates/exports, no span/trace exists.
findings.defense: A local dict can teach desired fields before introducing infrastructure.
findings.fix: Separate structured log record, metric recorder and trace/span stub with executable correlation tests.

findings.summary: A custom corr string is treated as sufficient trace evidence.
findings.attack: OpenTelemetry correlates logs/traces using TraceId/SpanId/execution trace context; no span is created here.
findings.defense: A domain correlation_id is still useful across systems.
findings.fix: Teach corr as optional business correlation in addition to trace_id/span_id, not as a substitute for tracing.

findings.summary: pii_raw=False is a literal rather than an enforced log schema/redaction test.
findings.attack: A payload could contain email/phone while the flag remains False.
findings.defense: The nominal event dict currently contains no raw email/phone.
findings.fix: Allowlist log fields and test forbidden keys/patterns; do not use a boolean declaration as proof.

findings.summary: redact() preserves the first two characters of any string without field policy or minimization.
findings.attack: Masking semantics differ for email/phone/IDs and may still leak identity; OWASP recommends omission/de-identification when identity is unnecessary.
findings.defense: The example only aims to show that raw values should not be logged.
findings.fix: Prefer no direct identifier; otherwise use field-aware approved masking/pseudonymization and tests.

findings.summary: p95 and error_rate are handwritten scalar literals; no sample set, denominator or compliance window produces them.
findings.attack: The lesson cannot demonstrate p95, error rate or an SLO from operational data.
findings.defense: Simple numbers isolate threshold comparison.
findings.fix: Compute SLIs from a synthetic request window and record count/errors/latency samples and SLO window.

findings.summary: Any current SLI threshold violation immediately maps to freeze_nonurgent_deploys and is described as consuming/exhausting error budget.
findings.attack: Error budget is allowance over a defined SLO compliance window; one point miss is not identical to budget exhaustion, and a current pass does not restore spent budget.
findings.defense: Freeze-on-breach is conservative as a toy policy.
findings.fix: Track allowed bad events/time and consumed budget over the window; enact freeze only according to explicit policy after exhaustion/burn-rate condition.

findings.summary: Negative/non-finite SLI values are not rejected.
findings.attack: CE06: p95=-1 and error_rate=-0.1 yields slo_ok=True and ship_features.
findings.defense: Nominal example is valid.
findings.fix: Validate finite p95>=0 and 0<=error_rate<=1 plus non-empty denominators.

findings.summary: CKPT and APPLIED are module-global dict/set despite prose claiming restart-surviving durable stores.
findings.attack: A process crash erases both, violating the central gate.
findings.defense: Comments label production alternatives such as SQLite/os.replace.
findings.fix: Use an on-disk temp SQLite/file fixture, reopen from a new process/test instance and assert resume state.

findings.summary: make_checkpoint writes status=done before the side effect executes.
findings.attack: CE08: crash after checkpoint before effect makes restart skip an effect that never happened.
findings.defense: The current side effect is only a list append and the happy-path test does not crash.
findings.fix: Define transactional state transitions; do not persist done until the operation/effect contract is durably resolved.

findings.summary: APPLIED.add(key) executes before side_effects.append(step).
findings.attack: If APPLIED were durable, crash between them suppresses all future retries while effect never occurred; AWS calls for atomic token+mutation semantics.
findings.defense: With an in-memory list/set the statements are adjacent.
findings.fix: Use atomic DB/outbox/inbox transaction or an external idempotent API keyed by the same operation identity.

findings.summary: Because key/checkpoint stores are in memory, a successful external effect followed by process death loses dedup state.
findings.attack: CE09 shows new process sees empty stores and may repeat the effect.
findings.defense: A real durable store is named in prose but not implemented.
findings.fix: Persist dedup/outcome atomically or reconcile against idempotent provider response before replay.

findings.summary: if key not in APPLIED followed by APPLIED.add is not a cross-worker atomic claim.
findings.attack: Two workers can both observe absent and execute the side effect; free-threaded/multiprocess execution makes reliance on interpreter serialization invalid.
findings.defense: Single-thread demo cannot race.
findings.fix: Use UNIQUE key/INSERT-if-absent transaction or compare-and-set in durable store and race-test two workers.

findings.summary: The only side effect is append to an in-memory list.
findings.attack: It cannot prove behavior against the real irreversible boundary the prose names: send/write/spend/review ticket.
findings.defense: Synthetic side effects avoid unsafe external actions.
findings.fix: Use a safe local durable sink (SQLite/outbox/file) with unique constraint and induced crash points.

findings.summary: Unknown step names are persisted as done and resume to themselves.
findings.attack: CE07 shows silent acceptance rather than controlled failure/quarantine.
findings.defense: Only known steps occur in nominal fixture.
findings.fix: Validate state/transition enums and fail closed on unknown state/version.

findings.summary: case:step:ver is taught as stable but the contract does not state whether ver is workflow intent version pinned to the item or current deployment version.
findings.attack: A late retry after deploy could receive a new key and repeat an old logical operation.
findings.defense: Including version can correctly distinguish genuinely different intended operations.
findings.fix: Persist operation/workflow version with the original work item and reuse it for retries; create new identity only for new intent.

findings.summary: route() retries every kind except literal poison until attempts expire.
findings.attack: CE10: permanent/validation/auth/business errors become retry, contradicting transient-only prose and potentially amplifying failures.
findings.defense: The toy only names poison/retriable in prose.
findings.fix: Use explicit retriable error classes/statuses and fail closed/DLQ/handoff for unknown or permanent failures.

findings.summary: DLQ and replay are route strings only.
findings.attack: No message body hash, failure reason, attempt count, first/last timestamps, idempotency key, code/version or controlled replay exists.
findings.defense: The lesson avoids deploying a broker.
findings.fix: Implement a local durable dead-letter table/list artifact with metadata and one-at-a-time replay after explicit fix/version selection.

findings.summary: runbook evidence is print('runbook', True).
findings.attack: No symptoms/checks/actions artifact exists or can be drilled/versioned.
findings.defense: The surrounding prose describes what a runbook should contain.
findings.fix: Provide/version a small Markdown/JSON runbook and execute at least one synthetic drill linked to observed evidence.

findings.summary: Executable backoff has no cap/deadline/jitter and accepts negative attempt/base.
findings.attack: CE11 produces a positive wait for negative attempt and a negative wait for negative base; unbounded 2**attempt can explode.
findings.defense: Prose explicitly says jitter in prod and max attempts is handled separately.
findings.fix: Validate domain, add capped/truncated backoff plus jitter/deadline policy, while keeping deterministic RNG in tests.

findings.summary: Prose shows delays for attempts 0..3 while route with max_attempts=3 sends attempt 3 directly to DLQ.
findings.attack: It is unclear whether max_attempts counts initial attempt or retries and whether the fourth delay is ever used.
findings.defense: Either convention can be valid if defined.
findings.fix: Define attempt/retry numbering once and derive waits/routes from that contract.

findings.summary: Despite systematic pytest being required from S27, theory has no collected tests for queue overflow, timeout cancellation, retry classification, process reopen or idempotency races.
findings.attack: Happy-path prints/asserts cannot stop regressions in the operational gate.
findings.defense: Some snippets contain Python assert statements.
findings.fix: Add pytest with induced crash/reopen and concurrent duplicate race tests plus invalid-input cases.

findings.summary: Tagline/gate promises trace per case, queue metrics and tested slow-provider/process-crash/reexecution handling, but the artifacts are mostly literals/classifiers/in-memory state.
findings.attack: Each named failure mode lacks an end-to-end executable demonstration.
findings.defense: All concepts appear in prose.
findings.fix: Create one integrated local harness that queues cases, induces slow call and process crash, reopens store, resumes once, emits trace/metrics and validates no duplicate effect.

findings.summary: Theory playground only constructs an idempotency-key string and prints pii_raw=False; it has no dedup store, atomic claim or restart.
findings.attack: A learner can infer that naming a key is equivalent to idempotence.
findings.defense: The playground is explicitly a compact practice surface.
findings.fix: Use a safe durable local store and actual duplicate/restart test, or label key construction as syntax only.

findings.summary: No experiment jointly reports throughput, latency distribution, timeout/error rate, queue depth/backpressure and resource saturation as concurrency changes.
findings.attack: Higher concurrency can increase throughput while destroying p95, error rate or memory/CPU; current lesson cannot detect that tradeoff.
findings.defense: Individual concepts are taught separately.
findings.fix: Add controlled load matrix N-workers×queue/rate settings and report all operational metrics under same manifest.

findings.summary: Parallelism/retries do not test preservation of candidate/ranking order, tie policy, duplicate handling or review destination inherited from triage.
findings.attack: Concurrency can reorder completion and retries can duplicate/miss work while all local snippets remain green.
findings.defense: S38 focuses on operational mechanics rather than model semantics.
findings.fix: Carry an artifact-specific oracle from S37/S39 boundary and assert keyed outputs/routes independent of completion order.

findings.summary: The section introduces threads/processes but never defines ownership/synchronization for mutable model/reference/cache state.
findings.attack: Shared mutable NumPy/cache state can race; process workers can instead silently fork stale copies.
findings.defense: Current toy examples barely share meaningful state.
findings.fix: Add explicit rule: immutable/read-only shared reference or per-worker copy; synchronize intentional mutation and test deterministic semantics.

USABLE: Bounded queues can provide backpressure by item count.
Queue.full() is advisory; put_nowait+Full or timed put is the correct atomic enqueue result signal.
Default GIL-enabled CPython limits pure-Python bytecode parallelism, while threads remain useful for I/O.
ProcessPoolExecutor can bypass the GIL but requires picklable work and has serialization/IPC cost.
Timeouts/cancellation/resource cleanup are necessary contracts for external I/O.
Logs, metrics and traces are distinct observability signals; correlation is necessary but not sufficient for tracing.
Idempotency identity should represent the logical operation, not each retry attempt.
Retries should be bounded and limited to retriable/transient failures.
DLQ replay should be controlled rather than bulk blind reinjection.
PARTIAL: SLI/SLO window calculation and error-budget accounting.
Runbook drills and integrated failure harness.
MISCONCEPTION_RISK: CPU-bound in CPython always means threads cannot help.
Vectorized NumPy scoring should automatically use processes.
json.dumps byte length measures ProcessPool IPC cost.
A token counter without refill is a per-window rate limiter.
Comparing latency_ms to timeout_s performs timeout/cancellation.
closed=True proves a resource was closed.
A correlation_id string is a trace.
pii_raw=False proves logs contain no PII.
Any instantaneous SLO miss means the error budget is exhausted.
Persisting done/token before side effect is safe idempotency.
check-then-add on a set is an atomic distributed claim.
